answer:
The author of *Paenitentiam Agere* is Pope John XXIII (Angelo Giuseppe Roncalli). He died in Rome, which was not its own country until 1929.

Rome became an independent sovereign state known as the "Italian Vatican State" or more commonly just Vatican City on February 11, 1929, when it was established by the Lateran Treaty between Italy and the Holy See.

Answer: 1929

_**Paenitentiam Agere**_ ("Penance for sins") was the seventh encyclical made by Pope John XXIII, and was issued on 1 July 1962. It calls on Christians to practice penance and considers the upcoming Second Vatican Council.

## Overview
Calls the Church to conversion, prayer, and penance in preparation for the Second Vatican Council.

## Why This Document Matters
It places ecclesial renewal within repentance and spiritual preparation rather than institutional planning alone.

## Historical Context
Issued by St. John XXIII in 1962, this papal encyclical addresses the pastoral, doctrinal, or governing needs of its period while remaining part of the Church's continuing documentary tradition.

## Authority and Status
Genre Papal Encyclical
Authority class Papal encyclical
Juridical force Doctrinal and pastoral
Current status Current
Promulgated 1962-07-01
Authoritative papal teaching; the weight of individual statements depends on their wording, subject, continuity, and intent.

Spirituality & Prayer Moral Theology Ecclesiology

steps.text:
The author of *Paenitentiam Agere* is Pope John XXIII (Angelo Giuseppe Roncalli). He died in Rome, which was not its own country until 1929.

Rome became an independent sovereign state known as the "Italian Vatican State" or more commonly just Vatican City on February 11, 1929, when it was established by the Lateran Treaty between Italy and the Holy See.

Answer: 1929
